title: Would
subtitle: One small word, several everyday jobs: polite requests, hypotheticals, and past habits.
objectives: Use "would" in the result clause of hypothetical (second/third) conditionals
Use "would" for repeated past habits (like "used to", for actions not states)

content.intro: "Would" shows up constantly in everyday English, doing several different, related jobs — this lesson pulls them all together.

rules.heading: a) Polite requests
rules.body:
• Would you please send me the report? (more polite than "will you")
  • Would you mind if I opened the window?

rules.heading: b) Hypotheticals (conditionals)
rules.body:
• If I were rich, I would buy a yacht. (second conditional)
  • They would have avoided the accident if they had been more careful. (third conditional)

rules.heading: c) Repeated past habits (actions, not states)
rules.body:
• When I was younger, I would visit my grandmother every summer. (a repeated action)
  • Not for states: use "used to," not "would," for things like "I used to have long hair" (not an action).

examples: Would you please send me the report by tomorrow?
If I were rich, I would buy a yacht and sail around the world.
She would speak five languages fluently, if she'd kept practicing.
When I was a child, I would play outside every afternoon.
They would have avoided the accident if they had been more careful.
Would you mind if I opened the window?

commonMistakes.wrong: When I was younger, I would have brown hair.
commonMistakes.right: When I was younger, I used to have brown hair.
commonMistakes.why: "Would" describes repeated actions, not states (like having a hair color) — use "used to" for states.

commonMistakes.wrong: If I was rich, I would buy a yacht.
commonMistakes.right: If I were rich, I would buy a yacht.
commonMistakes.why: The hypothetical "if" clause uses "were," not "was," for this fixed expression.

commonMistakes.wrong: Would you mind if I open the window?
commonMistakes.right: Would you mind if I opened the window?
commonMistakes.why: After "would you mind if," use the past simple form, even though the meaning is present/future.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct form using would.

items.prompt: ___ you please send me the report by tomorrow?
If I were rich, I ___ (buy) a yacht.
items.explanation: The result clause of the second conditional.

items.prompt: When I was a child, I ___ (play) outside every afternoon.
They ___ (avoid) the accident if they had been more careful.
items.explanation: The result clause of the third conditional.

items.prompt: When I was younger, I ___ brown hair. (a state, not an action)
items.explanation: States (having a hair color) need "used to," not "would."

items.prompt: ___ you mind if I opened the window?
items.explanation: "Would you mind if..." is the standard polite request form.

items.incorrect: When I was young, I would be tall for my age.
answer: When I was young, I was tall for my age.
items.explanation: A state (being tall) can't use "would" — just use the simple past.

items.incorrect: If I was you, I would apologize.
answer: If I were you, I would apologize.
items.explanation: Use "were," not "was," in this fixed hypothetical expression.

summary: Would appears in the result clause of second/third conditionals.
Would describes repeated past actions (not states — use "used to" for those).
